prompt:

Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

New part:
S538: The Performance Analytics Warehouse compares escalated exceptions with actual off-block performance to tune severity thresholds and reduce nuisance alerts over time.
S539: During Adverse Weather Mode or Capacity Reduction State, the Business Rules Registry can tighten escalation thresholds for flights close to departure while continuing to suppress low-impact local issues.
S540: If the Regional Flow Platform enters Contingency Fallback State, exception summaries remain available through the Contingency Operations Console with the same role-based visibility rules.
S541: The Data Governance Steward ensures that baggage and handler data exposed outside the local operation is limited to operational necessity and does not disclose unnecessary passenger or workforce details.
S542: Remote stands are used as controlled capacity buffers when contact gates are unavailable, when tow-in sequencing is more efficient than gate holding, or when an aircraft must wait clear of the terminal pier.
S543: The operational concept treats each remote stand as an airside resource with a landside service dependency, not as an isolated parking position.
S544: The Airport Duty Manager publishes the planned remote stand operating posture in the Airport CDM Portal before the first affected arrival bank.
S545: The Ramp Control Lead confirms that each planned remote stand has an assigned aircraft route, safe passenger transfer path, and defined contingency for blocked apron movement.
S546: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses remote stands to protect connection banks only when the resulting passenger transfer time is compatible with the planned departure sequence.
S547: Handling Resource Planner produces the Remote Stand Shuttle Count at regular operating intervals to represent available passenger transfer capacity for remote stand activity.
S548: Shuttle availability is modeled as a finite resource that includes vehicles, drivers, loading positions, terminal curb space, and accessible boarding support.
S549: Passenger bus constraints include maximum load, door cycle time, stand access routing, security segregation, mobility assistance requirements, and the time needed to clear passengers from the aircraft vicinity.
S550: The Ground Handling Dispatcher verifies that bus assignments do not conflict with baggage, catering, fueling, or crew transport movements on the same apron corridor.
S551: The Ramp Movement Board displays remote stand occupancy, expected towing actions, and bus service readiness in a shared view for airside coordination.
S552: The Tower Sequence Manager does not advance an aircraft toward an active departure sequence unless the remote stand release time supports the expected taxi plan.
S553: The Departure Metering Service incorporates remote stand constraints when estimating whether a Target Off Block Time remains achievable.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
